events.title: From Prince of Travel to Age of Abundance: Fireside Chat with Ricky Zhang
events.venue: FUNK. Coffee Bar, 1025 Dunsmuir St, Vancouver, BC V7X 1M5, Canada
events.description: Ricky Zhang spent years building a travel business and seeing much of the world along the way. Stepping back from it gave him time to dig into questions he had been putting off: why the world's most pressing problems are not on track to being solved, why hard work no longer seems to get people ahead, and what happens to jobs and savings as AI starts doing more of the work. The answers kept leading him back to the same place: the money itself. That search led him to Bitcoin, and in 2026 he started Age of Abundance, a weekly live show about the shift happening underneath the headlines in money, AI, energy, and humanity. Ricky believes we’re living through a one-time change for our species. For all of history, whoever controlled money could make more of it for themselves. Bitcoin is the first money nobody can do that to. Together with AI and cheaper energy, he sees it leading to a world where technology ushers in abundance for all. In this conversation, Ricky talks about how he came to Bitcoin, why AI makes honest money matter more than ever, and how each of us can help the people around us see what’s changing.

events.title: Vancouver AI Meetup: Where Humans Go, Where AI Goes
events.venue: H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, 1100 Chestnut St, Vancouver, BC V6J 3J9, Canada
events.description: On Wednesday, November 25, 2026, Vancouver AI is back under the dome at the H.R. MacMillan Space Centre. This month we hand the stage to a designer who has spent fifteen years deciding where people belong in a system, and where the machines do. Where humans go, where AI goes Most AI conversations start with the model. This one starts with judgement. Zoë Zaslow has spent fifteen years in product design, including design problems that were literally life and death. AI and natural language processing showed up in some of that work. They helped. They were never enough on their own. "The thing you need is judgement. Human judgement." That's Zoë's whole argument, and it's harder to practise than it sounds. AI doesn't solve the problem. It enables solutions. The real work is figuring out where human judgement has to sit, so you know where to put people and where to put AI. Zoë Zaslow. Photo: Michelle Diamond. The talk, in two parts Part one, 25 minutes. Fifteen years of design practice boiled down to four takeaways. Design process and systems thinking for people who build products but were never taught design thinking. Real cases, plain language, no jargon test at the door. Part two, 20 minutes. One project, start to finish. Where the people went, where the machines went, and why. Nobody gets scolded for shipping fast. Zoë's approach is gentle and Socratic: lead the room to the water and let it drink. Bring these questions Where does human judgement belong in the thing you're building, and where is it missing right now? When has AI actually earned its place in your work, and when did it fall short on its own? How do you design for a decision you can't afford to get wrong? You'll leave with four takeaways you can use on Monday, and a clearer way to decide what a person should own and what a model can carry. The Lineup Zoë Zaslow: Design strategist Fifteen years of product design, some of it on problems where a bad call could cost a life. Zoë works where design process meets systems thinking: the place a team decides what a person has to own and what a machine can carry. Kris Krüg: Executive Director, BC + AI Ecosystem Host and MC. Keeper of the vibe. Puller of threads. Kris opens the night with the community announcements: what's moving across BC + AI, who needs a hand, and where to plug in. The Flow Date: Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Time: 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM, Vancouver time Venue: H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, 1100 Chestnut St, Vancouver, BC V6J 3J9 Getting there: the #2 and #32 buses stop a 5-minute walk away, and the False Creek Ferry drops off at Vanier Park. Pay parking is in Lot 60 (EasyPark, by app or kiosk). It's a 10-minute walk from Granville Island. 6:00 PM, doors: open networking. Find the people you came for, and a few you didn't. 7:00 PM, program: community announcements, then Zoë. Questions and the open floor after. Until 10:00 PM: more networking and productive arguing about the future. Photos and video: the night is photographed and recorded for the community archive. If you'd rather stay out of frame, tell a volunteer at the door. Questions or access needs: kk@bc-ai.ca More of the program will be posted as it's confirmed. Come late. Leave early. Nobody keeps score. Other Upcoming Events in Our Community AI Ethical Futures Lab #9CV + AI Community Meetup #7: Trust The Room, Question The MachineFV + AI November: Fraser Valley AI Community MeetupAI Film Club with Kevin Friel | Nov 12BC + AI Life Sciences: AI in the clinic, part 2ED + AI #15: What It Gave Back, What It TookAI Happy Hour at FriendsQuarters #7: Heads Down, Look UpVancouver AI Community Meetup: 12/16 Plug into the bigger organism This meetup is part of the BC + AI Ecosystem Association, a member-driven nonprofit where meetups turn into working groups, prototypes turn into shared tools, and community values turn into governance. Join or support BC + AI See you Nov 25. 🖤❤️✊ Kris Krüg & the Vancouver AI Community The Sponsors Big thanks to the folks helping keep the lights on, the doors open, and the community infrastructure real: Intellomx: Simon Haworth's crew is building an AI-powered drug discovery platform across transcriptomic, genomic, and proteomic data. Deep science, local roots, real support for the ecosystem. Internet Archive Canada: Andrea Mills and the crew at The Permanent are preserving decades of the open internet while more knowledge disappears behind paywalls. They are also co-creating the Archive Builders Micro-Fellowship with us. Community Partners H.R. MacMillan Space Centre: Our venue partner and monthly home under the dome. They keep opening the doors and letting a strange mix of technologists, artists, and curious neighbours turn a planetarium into an emerging-tech commons. Metacreation Lab for Creative AI: Professor Philippe Pasquier and his lab at SFU's School of Interactive Arts & Technology have been pushing computational creativity long before it became fashionable. CreativeMornings Vancouver: More than a decade of building Vancouver's creative community and cross-pollinating the people who make this city interesting. Ethọ́s Lab: Vancouver's Black and Indigenous youth-led studio where young people ship real products, experiment with creative technology, and build futures on their own terms. About Vancouver AI Vancouver AI is a neural network of curious humans mapping the terrain between technology and consciousness. We bridge art galleries and research labs, corporate towers and garage workshops because the future does not get built in one kind of room. We run monthly gatherings where builders, researchers, artists, educators, founders, and students trade demos, tools, ethics, and hard questions. No outside agenda. Just a self-organizing community that gives a damn about where this revolution goes and who gets to steer. About BC + AI Ecosystem Association BC + AI is the province-wide layer: a community-driven nonprofit building public-interest infrastructure for AI in British Columbia. Not a corporate lobby. Not a think tank. A commons where local meetups turn into working groups, prototypes, shared tools, member connections, and a stronger public voice for people doing the work. Vancouver AI was the first node. The ecosystem now reaches across BC, with every community bringing its own culture, needs, and experiments. Code of Care Be kind. Be curious. This is a harassment-free, consent-first room. Credit people. Share code, notes, photos, and ideas with attribution. Ask before filming or recording any person, conversation, or screen. Make space. Help new people into the conversation and leave room for perspectives that do not sound like yours. Get Involved The meetup gets better when the community brings the sparks. We are always looking for volunteers, speakers, sponsors, demos, photographers, and people who know how to make a room feel alive. Bring a demo, join BC + AI, or show up with an idea and find the people who can help you move it.

events.venue: The Pint Public House, 455 Abbott St, Vancouver, BC V6B 2L2, Canada
events.description: Once upon a time, back in 2014, in a faraway land known as Vancouver, a little tradition was born. In those days, when cloud computing was still young, there was a fellow who hosted monthly cloud gatherings at Lighthouse Labs and CodeCore in the magical neighbourhood of Gastown. Before each gathering, this fellow could always be found at The Pint, frantically finishing that evening's presentation. He never invited anyone to join him, for there were slides to finish and precious little time. But word spread, and one by one, familiar faces began appearing. A quick hello became a conversation, a conversation became a new friendship, and before long, his quiet preparation time had become a gathering of its own. And so he learned an important lesson: the fewer slides he prepared, the better the conversations became. Then, one December in 2016, a brilliant idea struck him. Or perhaps it was simply laziness disguised as brilliance. "What if," he wondered, "instead of preparing another presentation, I invited all of Vancouver's tech user groups to celebrate the year together?" And so, a new annual tradition was born. The years passed. Technologies rose and fell, friendships flourished, and the tradition grew. Even a great plague that swept across the land could only interrupt the festivities for a little while. Ten years after that first December gathering, the tradition continues where it all began. The Pint. And this year, half the pub will once again be transformed into a gathering place for Vancouver's tech community, filled with familiar faces, new connections, music, and a little festive magic. No slide decks. No demos. Just good people, great conversations, and a celebration of the community we've built together. And the best part of this fairy tale? Everyone is invited to be part of the next chapter. 🎄 Here's what awaits you: 🤝 An opportunity to meet and connect with people from across Vancouver's tech communities 🎧 A DJ bringing the music and festive atmosphere 🎁 Prizes and giveaways throughout the evening 🎤 A few brief words from the sponsors who help make our community events possible 🎉 Half of The Pint reserved exclusively for our gathering Wednesday, December 9, 2026 6:00 PM onwards The Pint, Vancouver Whether you're a developer, architect, student, community organizer, tech leader, or simply someone curious about technology, there's a place for you here. Come on your own or bring a friend. Reconnect with familiar faces, meet people from communities you haven't explored yet, share stories, exchange ideas, and perhaps make a connection that leads to something wonderful. No presentations to sit through. No technical debates to win. Just a chance to celebrate the people who make Vancouver's tech community what it is. Because the best part of the tech community has never been the technology. It's always been the people. And as for how our story ends? Well, that's something we'll write together. See you there! ✨
